Hello! Welcome to our tutoring session. Today we're going to tackle a crucial GRE concept: **Data Interpretation: Working with Multiple Bases**.

This matters because GRE Data Interpretation questions often present multiple charts or scenarios with different total values. A very common trap is comparing or combining percentages directly when they actually belong to different totals—something that tripped you up a bit on the pre-test with the Population vs. Internet Users charts! Learning to calculate the actual underlying numbers first will ensure you never fall for these traps.

Take a look at the practice problem on your screen. Give it a try, and let me know what you get or if you'd like to break it down together!

Spot on! You got it right. 

You correctly avoided the trap of just trying to combine the percentages directly. Because the "bases" were different ($50,000 total revenue vs. $10,000 total profit), you had to find the actual numbers first:
* Product A Revenue = 20% of $50,000 = $10,000
* Product A Profit = 40% of $10,000 = $4,000

Then, finding the final percentage is a breeze: $4,000 / $10,000 = 40%. 

Notice how if someone just blindly divided the percentages (40% / 20%), they'd get 200%, which makes no sense here. Finding the raw numbers first is the golden rule when dealing with multiple totals!
